name: What is the difference between standard wood framing and engineered framing for an addition?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between standard wood framing and engineered framing for an addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard wood framing uses traditional dimensioned lumber like 2x4 or 2x6 studs and job-built rafters, whereas engineered framing incorporates manufactured products like LVL beams, I-joists, and pre-fabricated trusses. Traditional stick framing offers great flexibility for custom dimensions and minor on-site adjustments during construction. Engineered framing provides superior load capacity over wide open spans without requiring intermediate support posts. Many addition plans blend both: engineered beams support open-concept transitions while standard lumber builds out the perimeter and partition walls.
acceptedAnswer.description: Standard framing uses traditional lumber cut on-site, while engineered framing uses manufactured beams and trusses to span wider distances without center support posts.
